Subject: PHI routing & BAA availability — CardioMed follow-up

Hi Alex / CardioMed security team,

Thanks again for the call this morning — quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment: 

Summary from call:
- CardioMed will be routing PHI into the app as part of triage flows (care notes + structured vitals).
- Primary question: can Redwood accept PHI, and if so, which hosting modes are eligible (Hosted API vs Dedicated vs Private)?
- You asked for SOC 2 status and a vendor security questionnaire to start the intake.

Redwood posture / immediate answers:
- SOC 2: Redwood has a Type II in-progress; summary report (controls scope + estimated delivery) is attached as redwood-soc2-summary.pdf. Full report available under NDA — we can provide next week if needed.
- PHI handling: We do not recommend placing PHI on the shared Hosted API in current configuration. Eligible deployment modes for PHI are Dedicated (reserved GPU pools with customer isolation) and Private (VPC/on-prem). Both support BAA execution.
- BAA: we can sign a standard BAA. I've attached a draft cardiomed-baa-template.docx to accelerate redlines — our legal prefers to start from your template if you have one.

Immediate asks / next steps:
1) Alex/security team: confirm whether you prefer Dedicated or Private for POC (we can spin a small Dedicated sandbox within 5 business days).
2) Please complete the vendor security questionnaire attached (vendor-security-questionnaire.xlsx) and return to security@redwood.com; Vanessa will own intake.
3) If you want the SOC 2 Type II report, send an NDA link or let us know and we will share under access controls.
4) Proposed next touch: technical security POC with our infra engineer (Rishi) — are you available next week for a 30-minute deep dive?

I will follow up internally to assign owners. Thanks again — noted items are actionable and time-boxed below.

—
Sergio Alvarez
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
sergio@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0198
